title: OneDrive and SharePoint: single hero link for file and folder sharing
summary: Hold: the site-default command omits a qualification in its reference that matters for group-connected sites. The reference's list of valid parameters for Groups site collections excludes DefaultMainLinkScope; the briefing should surface that uncertainty rather than recommend the command without qualification.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on 7 October 2026.
Each OneDrive or SharePoint file or folder has one hero link in the new sharing experience.
claims.quote: In OneDrive and SharePoint, each item has one hero link.

claims.claim: Users can change the hero link's audience and permissions without creating a new URL.
claims.quote: A hero link allows users to share a single link for an item, then change the audience and permissions for that link without needing to create a new URL.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Add people remains a separate means of granting direct access.
claims.quote: Users can share an item with specific people or security groups through Add people. This action grants direct access to the item.

claims.claim: MC1454378 calls this the third-generation Microsoft 365 sharing experience.
claims.quote: We're introducing the third-generation Microsoft 365 sharing experience to make collaboration simpler, smarter, and more secure by default.

claims.claim: The sharing experience applies to copied links, email sharing and the browser URL.
claims.quote: Users will see one consistent sharing experience whether they copy a link, share through email, or use the browser URL.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The hero link's default audience is Only people added to the file.
claims.quote: By default, the hero link is set to Only people added to the file, meaning the link itself does not grant access to anyone.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Only people added to the file grants no additional access and is the narrowest starting audience.
claims.quote: At this scope, the link works for people who already have access, such as through a direct permission, a group, or the parent folder or site. It grants no additional access.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Users can broaden the hero link to organisation members or, where policy permits, anyone with the link.
claims.quote: Users can broaden access to people in the organization with the link or, where permitted by organizational policy, to anyone with the link.

claims.claim: Users can select view, edit or view without downloading, subject to available permissions.
claims.quote: Users can choose whether recipients can view, edit, or view without downloading, depending on available permissions.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A sender can widen access for a recipient on the same hero link without redistributing a URL.
claims.quote: If recipients cannot open a previously shared file, the sender can expand access on the same hero link without redistributing a new URL.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Existing sharing links keep working and appear under Other links.
claims.quote: Links created before the hero link sharing experience continue to work and appear under Other links.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Users see a tutorial the first time they open the new sharing dialog.
claims.quote: Users will see a tutorial experience upon opening the new share dialog for the first time.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Can view is the default when users first grant access through the hero link.
claims.quote: Can view is the default when a user first allows access to an item through the hero link.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Administrators cannot configure a different default hero link permission.
claims.quote: Administrators can't configure a different default permission for the hero link.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Audience or permission changes affect links already sent, including limiting their use when the scope narrows.
claims.quote: Changing the scope or permission doesn't create a new URL. The change applies to links already sent, so narrowing the scope limits who can use those links.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: A file inherits its folder's hero link settings until its own hero link is explicitly set or changed.
claims.quote: A file inherits its folder's hero link settings until the file's own hero link is explicitly set or changed. After that, the file's hero link settings are independent.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Hero-link-specific licensing has not been published, so the feature's licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint OneDrive hero link licensing license pricing meter billing DefaultMainLinkScope. Opened shareable-links-anyone-specific-people-organization, SharePoint service description, roadmap and MC1454378; no hero-link-specific licensing rule found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No pay-as-you-go or credit meter is documented specifically for the hero link at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint OneDrive hero link licensing license pricing meter billing DefaultMainLinkScope. Read feature page, SharePoint service description, roadmap, MC1454378 and billing search results; no hero-link meter found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing internal sharing guidance and end-user documentation.
claims.quote: Review internal sharing guidance and end-user documentation to reflect the new single-link sharing model.

claims.claim: No admin UI for setting the site hero link default audience is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint hero link DefaultMainLinkScope admin center configure default audience tenant UI; "hero link" "admin center" "DefaultMainLinkScope". Opened feature, Set-SPOSite and default-sharing-link pages; no hero-link admin UI found.

claims.where: controls[0].api; summary; Scope: Configuration; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site URL> -DefaultMainLinkScope <OnlyPeopleAdded|Organization|Anyone> is recommended for sites without a Groups-site qualification.
claims.quote: For Groups site collection, the only valid parameters are Identity, AllowSelfServiceUpgrade, DefaultLinkPermission, DefaultSharingLinkType, DenyAddAndCustomizePages, DisableCompanyWideSharingLinks, DisableSharingForNonOwners, FileAnonymousLinkType, FolderAnonymousLinkType, LockState, Owner, ResourceQuota
claims.fix: Keep the documented command, but add to controls[0].note and the site-default guidance: 'The Set-SPOSite reference also omits DefaultMainLinkScope from its list of valid parameters for Groups site collections; support for those sites is unconfirmed.' Qualify the summary as 'admins can set a site default with DefaultMainLinkScope, subject to the site-type documentation gaps below.' Do not recommend it unconditionally for group-connected sites. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/sharepoint-online/set-sposite.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Running Set-SPOSite requires both SharePoint Online administrator and site collection administrator rights.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Online administrator and be a site collection administrator to run the cmdlet.

claims.claim: DefaultMainLinkScope sets a starting audience rather than preventing users from broadening it where policy permits.
claims.quote: DefaultMainLinkScope controls only the default audience and does not prevent users from broadening access when allowed by policy.

claims.claim: OneDrive support is uncertain because the notice explicitly includes it but the reference's exclusive OneDrive parameter list omits DefaultMainLinkScope.
claims.quote: For OneDrive for Business site collection, the only valid parameters are Identity, AllowDownloadingNonWebViewableFiles, AllowEditing, ConditionalAccessPolicy, DefaultLinkPermission, DefaultSharingLinkType, DisableCompanyWideSharingLinks, FileAnonymousLinkType, FolderAnonymousLinkType, LimitedAccessFileType

claims.where: controls[1].ui and api; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: There is no documented tenant-wide equivalent of the hero link audience default on either administrative surface.
claims.quote: Searched: "hero link" "tenant" "default" Set-SPOTenant; "hero link" "admin center" "DefaultMainLinkScope". Read Set-SPOTenant and feature page; MC1454378 explicitly says there is currently no tenant-wide equivalent setting.

claims.claim: The Set-SPOTenant reference lists no main link parameter at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched fetched Set-SPOTenant text for MainLink, main link and hero: no matches. Also searched Learn: "hero link" "tenant" "default" Set-SPOTenant; results expose legacy defaults, not a main-link parameter.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Organisation-level external sharing is configured in SharePoint admin center > Policies > Sharing.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Policies, and then select Sharing.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -SharingCapability <value> sets the organisation-level sharing capability.
claims.quote:
### -SharingCapability

Determines what level of sharing is available for OneDrive and SharePoint sites.

claims.quote:
In the left column, select a site.
3. Select Sharing on the command bar.
4. Under Default sharing link type, clear the Same as organization-level setting checkbox.

The default link type for the site collection. To be replaced by DefaultShareLinkScope.

claims.where: controls[2].note; What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The organisation's sharing policies determine the hero link scopes available to users.
claims.quote: The audience scope determines who can use the hero link. Available scopes depend on the organization's sharing policies.

claims.claim: Anyone with the link can use that scope without signing in.
claims.quote: Anyone who receives the link can use it without signing in, including people outside the organization.

claims.claim: Anonymous use of Anyone links cannot be audited to a named user.
claims.quote: Anyone can forward the link, and anonymous use can't be audited to a named user.

claims.claim: Selecting a broader scope does not by itself make content searchable or available through Copilot to everyone.
claims.quote: Selecting this scope doesn't grant organization-wide access or make the item available in search or Copilot for everyone in the organization. Access through the link is established when a recipient redeems it.

claims.claim: Directly added users and security group members can discover the item in search and access it through Copilot, subject to permissions.
claims.quote: The item can appear in search results and is accessible through Copilot for selected users and security group members, subject to their permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Effective access is the highest permission granted by direct access, groups, inheritance or any sharing link.
claims.quote: A user's effective access is the highest permission granted by any source: direct access, a group, the parent folder or site, the hero link, or another sharing link.

claims.claim: Resetting the hero link does not revoke permissions from other sources; those sources must also be changed to reduce access.
claims.quote: Reducing access requires changing each source that grants a higher permission.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Existing default sharing link settings and expiration policies continue to govern legacy links rather than hero links.
claims.quote: Existing default sharing link settings and link expiration policies continue to apply to legacy links and do not govern hero links.

claims.claim: The cited sources describe user-initiated sharing rather than autonomous or agent actions for this change.
claims.quote: Searched the supplied roadmap and MC1454378 and read the complete shareable-links feature page: actions are described as users adding people or changing link settings; no autonomous or agent behaviour is described.

claims.claim: MC1454378 lists OnlyPeopleAdded as the default and Organization as the other supported value.
claims.quote: Supported values are:- OnlyPeopleAdded (default)- Organization

claims.claim: The Set-SPOSite reference lists OnlyPeopleAdded, Organization and Anyone for DefaultMainLinkScope.
claims.quote:
The valid values are:
- OnlyPeopleAdded
- Organization
- Anyone

claims.claim: Anyone falls back to the next more restrictive default if Anyone links are disabled for the site.
claims.quote: Anyone is only available if anonymous links are allowed at the tenant level. If Anyone is selected but the site has Anyone links disabled, the effective default falls back to the next most restrictive value.

claims.claim: The DefaultMainLinkScope parameter applies to all items at the root of the document library.
claims.quote: The default audience for main links used in sharing. Applies to all items at the root of the document library. Only audience scope is set by this parameter.

claims.claim: The site audience default is the only documented administrative control specifically for the hero link itself.
claims.quote: Searched: "hero link" "controls" "PowerShell"; "hero link" "admin center" "DefaultMainLinkScope"; "hero link" "tenant" "default" Set-SPOTenant. Read feature, Set-SPOSite, Set-SPOTenant and MC1454378; no other hero-link-specific admin control found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a complete setting-by-setting mapping of sharing policies to hero link scope availability.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint hero link scopes sharing policies Anyone Organization control DefaultMainLinkScope. Read feature, external-sharing settings and Set-SPOSite; found the Anyone prerequisite and general policy dependency, not a complete scope mapping.

claims.claim: A site's sharing setting must be the same as or more restrictive than the organisation's setting.
claims.quote: Each site has its own sharing setting that you can set independently, though it must be at the same or more restrictive setting as the organization.

claims.claim: Every user who shares files will encounter the dialog during the November 2026 window whether or not administrators prepare.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rolling out early October 2026 (previously mid-September) through end of November 2026 (previously late October)
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with: 'Microsoft's notice schedules the new dialog to roll out from early October through the end of November 2026 without administrator action, so prepare users even if you do not change any settings.' This preserves the scheduled window rather than guaranteeing a November arrival for every user.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to take stock of legacy link expiration settings, but those settings have no controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Reconfirm what legacy default sharing link and expiration settings still cover'. The table includes default sharing link type, but no link expiration control.
claims.fix: Narrow that checklist bullet to 'Reconfirm what legacy default sharing link settings still cover, since the notice says they do not govern hero links.' Do not add a control row as part of this correction.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends communicating the updated sharing experience to regular collaborators.
claims.quote: Communicate the updated sharing experience to users who regularly collaborate across teams and organizations.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends evaluating site-level defaults where different sharing behaviours are needed.
claims.quote: Evaluate site-level default sharing settings where different sharing behaviors are required.

claims.claim: The Anyone value of DefaultMainLinkScope requires anonymous links to be allowed at tenant level.
claims.quote: Anyone is only available if anonymous links are allowed at the tenant level.

claims.claim: A recipient must receive and redeem the link before the shared content becomes searchable for that recipient.
claims.quote: A person must receive and redeem the link by selecting it before the shared content becomes searchable for them.

claims.claim: MC1454378 explicitly describes DefaultMainLinkScope as configurable at SharePoint site collection or OneDrive level.
claims.quote: Administrators can configure the default audience for the hero link at the SharePoint site collection or OneDrive level by using the DefaultMainLinkScope parameter in SharePoint PowerShell.
